system.title: Dynamical regime and parameter identification of a whole-brain MPR model from resting-state fMRI (r13)

planets.label: What resting-state BOLD determines about a whole-brain MPR model
planets.detail: Decide which dynamical regime, bistable or monostable, and which low-dimensional parameters (G, noise level, eta_0, a) of an MPR whole-brain model the resting-state BOLD of one subject determines.

evidence.quote: We ask what the resting-state BOLD of one subject determines about a whole-brain Montbrió–Pazó–Roxin (MPR) model

planets.label: Resting-state fMRI dynamics
planets.detail: Both configurations are fitted to the same real resting-state data by forward stochastic simulation and read against a linear model.

evidence.quote: fitted to the same real data by forward stochastic simulation

planets.label: Physics-informed neural networks
planets.detail: A network maps time to (r, V) of every region; the residuals of the MPR equations enter the loss.

evidence.quote: no PINN has been applied to the whole-brain MPR model with real BOLD

planets.label: Single-subject resting-state fMRI
planets.detail: Any instance with N regions and T volumes at TR; the instance of Section 3.1 is provisional and the synthetic stage decides the dataset.

evidence.quote: one subject of a resting-state dataset, parcellated into $N$ regions, with $T$ volumes at repetition time TR

planets.label: Undetermined dynamical regime and unreliable regional excitability
planets.detail: A regime or a parameter set that reproduces the data is not evidence unless the data determine it; the bistable regime of whole-brain MPR models is assumed before fitting.

evidence.quote: a parameter set or a regime that reproduces the data is not enough if the data do not determine it

planets.label: Bistable against monostable configuration of one biophysical model on real resting-state fMRI
planets.detail: The two configurations of the same MPR model are compared on the same data after a synthetic test of discriminability; to the authors' knowledge no earlier study does this.

evidence.quote: no study has compared a bistable and a monostable configuration of the same biophysical neural mass model on real resting-state fMRI

planets.label: Parameter inference for brain network models
planets.detail: Estimation of the parameters of a connectome-based model from neuroimaging data.

evidence.quote: Every parameter that is not estimated is fixed and declared.

planets.label: Synthetic identifiability and discriminability map
planets.detail: On synthetic data of each regime: which BOLD statistics identify the regime and recover the parameters, and at what number of volumes; required before any real-data result is read.

evidence.quote: it is established which statistics of the BOLD identify the regime and recover the parameters

planets.label: Low-dimensional regional parametrisation
planets.detail: eta_i = eta_0 + a m_i with a fixed regional map, estimated with G and the noise level; free eta_i kept as a control.

evidence.quote: the regional excitabilities are tied to a fixed map with two free parameters

planets.label: Regime comparison under equal conditions
planets.detail: Bistable and monostable configurations fitted to the same data with a sweep and CMA-ES, compared on held-out BOLD statistics, with a linear model as lower reference.

evidence.quote: the bistable and the monostable configuration are fitted to the same real data by forward stochastic simulation

planets.label: Hybrid PINN as estimator and reconstructor of regional states
planets.detail: The PINN is one estimator among those compared; its specific role is to reconstruct which state each region occupies. Its noise forcing term is owed in r13.

evidence.quote: its specific role is to reconstruct which state each region occupies over time

planets.label: Physics residual scales for hidden states
planets.detail: Equations non-dimensionalised; each residual divided by a fixed scale derived from the magnitude of the terms of its equation.

evidence.quote: each residual is divided by the sum of the absolute values of the terms of its equation

planets.label: FC fit read against ceilings and benchmarks
planets.detail: Expected, not yet measured: rho_FC against the seed ceiling, the session ceiling when available, and the sweep and CMA-ES fits.

evidence.quote: Success is read against the ceilings of Section 6

planets.label: Parameters interpreted only if identifiable
planets.detail: Expected, not yet measured: parameters are interpreted only after synthetic recovery and convergence across seeds and sessions.

evidence.quote: The parameters are called interpretable when three conditions hold.

pillars.label: Synthetic identifiability and discriminability map
pillars.detail: On synthetic BOLD generated in the bistable and in the monostable configuration, the statistics that identify the regime and recover the parameters are established before any real-data result is read; this stage also decides the dataset (Section 1, H1).

pillars.label: Low-dimensional regional parametrisation
pillars.detail: The regional excitabilities are tied to a fixed map with two free parameters (Eq. 15); the free regional model is only the control of H3. The parametrisation of the noise level is owed (Section 7).

pillars.label: Regime comparison under equal conditions
pillars.detail: Both configurations are fitted by forward stochastic simulation with a sweep and CMA-ES and compared on BOLD statistics held out from the fit, with a linear model as lower reference; either outcome is reported (H2).

pillars.label: Hybrid PINN as estimator and reconstructor of states
pillars.detail: Network weights and parameters are trained jointly with a differentiable Balloon-Windkessel forward model (Eqs. 14 to 23); the forcing term that represents the noise is owed (Section 7). H4 can fail without affecting H1 to H3.

hypotheses.statement: From BOLD generated in the bistable and in the monostable configuration, a declared set of BOLD statistics identifies the generating configuration and recovers G, the noise level, eta_0 and a within a declared tolerance at a stated number of volumes.

Fits of the bistable and of the monostable configuration to the same data differ in held-out BOLD statistics by more than the variability across seeds and sessions; either sign is reported, against a linear model as lower reference.
Repeated fitting with different seeds and initial values converges to the same values, and across sessions when the subject has two; with eta_i free in every region, as a control, it does not.

On synthetic data the hybrid PINN recovers the fraction of time each region spends in each state; on real data its parameters give a forward-simulated rho_FC no lower than a sweep and CMA-ES under a declared budget.
